sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Motion Picture International Copyright Distribution and Licensing

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Marshall Islands (Delap-Uliga-Darrit, Majuro Atoll registered office context)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: statutory corporate law modeled on Delaware General Corporation Law / US common law, with customary title and land law; unitary national legal system.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Title 26, Chapter 1, Sections 31 (Articles of Incorporation), 39 (Purpose), 40 (Registered Office and Agent), 48 (Bylaws), 59 (Directors), and 67 (Officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Registrar, Marshall Islands Corporate Registry, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (the official incorporation instrument filed for a Business Corporation under the Business Corporations Act).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account required. The Corporation may issue shares for such consideration as the Board determines, and the authorized capital is set in the Articles of Incorporation. In practice, a nominal issued capital of USD 1.00 is acceptable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Dated [Date]. The incorporator presented the Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED: that the share subscription be accepted and the initial directors elected; that the registered office at [Law firm address] in Majuro be adopted; that the following officers be appointed: President [Name] and Secretary/Treasurer [Name]; that the President be authorized to execute banking documents and retain the registered agent; and that all filings and licenses incidental to the Corporation's lawful film licensing operations be approved. The Secretary is directed to certify these resolutions and maintain corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Corporate Registry (online pre-clearance or in-person at Majuro).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the proposed corporate name, ensuring the name is distinctive and not misleadingly similar to any existing Marshall Islands entity. A letter of intent to reserve may be accepted. Name must include a corporate designator such as 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or allowable abbreviation.
required_dossiers: Statement confirming no existing identical or deceptively similar name
Consent to use corporate designator (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may resubmit an amended name or request administrative review by the Registrar. A properly requested alternate name is handled as a new reservation without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in the Marshall Islands or a notary recognized under Marshall Islands law; final filing with the Registrar of Corporations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in compliance with Section 31, including the Corporation name, authorized share structure, registered agent and registered office address, initial directors, and any lawful purpose clauses. The incorporator or authorized officer must execute the articles and have their signature notarized. If executed outside the Marshall Islands, the signature may be acknowledged before a notary public whose certificate is authenticated to the extent required by the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Duly executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation in English
Notarized acceptance of office by the registered agent, if applicable
Consent to act as initial director(s)
Power of attorney or authorization document if submitted by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or deficiency notice, the applicant may cure the defect by filing an amended document or supplemental affidavit. Rejected filings may be resubmitted within 30 days without forfeiting the filing fee, provided the statutory revision is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing, Fee Payment, and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Corporate Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles of Incorporation and pay the statutory filing fee of USD 200 by wire, bank draft, or other approved method. Upon acceptance, the Registrar will endorse the articles and issue a Certificate of Incorporation evidencing the Corporation's legal existence.
required_dossiers: Annual franchise tax pre-registration or acknowledgment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation is withheld or delayed, the applicant may request a written statement of grounds and lodge a formal appeal with the Registrar. A defective filing may be corrected by filing a certificate of correction within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Bylaws and Organizational Minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Directors / Shareholders of the Business Corporation; no government filing required, but must remain with the Corporation's statutory records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a virtual or written organizational meeting of the initial directors. Adopt the Corporate Bylaws, approve the share issuance to the subscriber, elect the initial directors, and approve any optional indemnity and share transfer restrictions. The minutes and bylaws must be kept at the registered office or principal records location.
required_dossiers: Initial director consent or online written resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer is unavailable to sign, the meeting may be postponed by written consent; all actions require majority approval. Withdrawal of a director requires immediate written replacement by the shareholder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Officers and Issuance of Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Board of Directors of the Business Corporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At the organizational meeting, the Board appoints the President and Secretary/Treasurer (or any officer designations provided in the Bylaws), fixes the authorized capital designated in the Articles, and issues share certificates to the subscriber. The Corporation ledger should reflect the number of shares and consideration paid.
required_dossiers: Share certificate stubs and registered share ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer fails to qualify, the Board may appoint a substitute by board resolution. A defective share issuance may be voided and reissued upon board ratification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Agent Confirmation and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry (for agent confirmation); any licensed bank in the Marshall Islands or international correspondent bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered agent has filed the statutory acceptance with the Registrar. Thereafter, present the Certificate of Incorporation, Bylaws, board resolution on banking authority, and officer identification to a financial institution to open corporate bank accounts. If the Corporation will operate wholly offshore, request non-resident business status confirmation for tax exemption purposes.
required_dossiers: Board resolution authorizing bank account opening
Certificate of Good Standing or registered agent confirmation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application due to deficient documentation, the Corporation may obtain a Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar and resubmit. A registered agent change may be filed with the Registrar and a new bank package issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies; the activity is offshore film copyright distribution and licensing. If physical premises are operated, the Majuro Atoll Local Government may require a general business license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not statutorily required for the Corporation's pure intellectual property licensing and distribution activity. An optional general business office permit may be obtained from the Majuro Atoll Local Government if a physical office is maintained.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – administrative and licensing activities do not trigger an Environmental Impact Assessment Report. A waiver or registration letter may be issued to confirm no prescribed discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the core activity. If an office is established, wastewater disposal must comply with RMI EPA Clean Water standards; no volatile organic compounds or industrial emissions are expected from film licensing operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required only if a physical office or storage facility is occupied. The Corporation must obtain a fire safety inspection clearance from the Office of the Chief Fire Officer, ensure structural load approval for any server or archival equipment storage, and maintain a workplace health and safety certificate in accordance with Marshall Islands Labor Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands – Revenue and Taxation Division (operational portal: https://www.rmi-finance.org)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Business Corporation (BC) obtains a corporate registration number from the Registrar of Corporations under the Business Corporations Act. No TIN or VAT ID is issued to a purely non-resident BC. If the BC later establishes a taxable presence in the Marshall Islands (e.g., local physical office, employees, or RMI-source business activity), it must apply for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) using the Revenue and Taxation Division registration forms. For independent film licensing conducted entirely offshore, no ministerial license and no local TIN is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone – non-resident domestic Business Corporation whose foreign-source income and offshore licensing royalties are outside the RMI income tax base
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election under RMI law. Under the Business Corporations Act, a corporation may elect non-resident status by filing the appropriate articles/registration with the Registrar of Corporations; this election confirms exemption from RMI income tax on non-RMI-source income. No deemed dividend or transparent pass-through election is available because the jurisdiction imposes no corporate income tax on non-resident BCs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/Sales and Use Tax – the Marshall Islands levies only customs import duties under the Customs Act; there is no general consumption tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable – no VAT/GST or sales tax registration threshold exists in the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, API reporting, or digital stamping regime is in force. RMI customs entry processing is administered through the Customs Service within the Ministry of Finance; paper or electronic declarations are accepted without third-party fiscal validation infrastructure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable – because RMI does not impose VAT/GST/sales tax, there is no export zero-rating mechanism and no VAT refund claim can arise. Film license royalties earned by a non-resident BC from foreign distributors are not RMI-source income and are exempt from RMI income tax under the non-resident domestic corporation rules. To maintain that exemption, the BC must not carry on trade or business in RMI and must derive the royalties from licensing activities wholly outside the islands.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable – no RMI VAT export zero-rating refund scheme exists; therefore no statutory VAT-claim customs documentation bundle is required.
Recommended if physical film prints are exported: RMI Customs export declaration, commercial invoice, and packing list.
Recommended for licensing-income substantiation: executed film license agreement, film title/rights schedule, and bill of lading or airway bill where physical media is moved.
Recommended for remittance substantiation: inward remittance certificate (SWIFT MT103/MT950) and bank statement evidencing receipt of royalties from the foreign licensee.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Not applicable in a VAT context because RMI has no VAT/GST and no zero-rating refund clawback mechanism. However, if a BC is found to have violated the non-resident conditions or misrepresented its offshore status, the Revenue and Taxation Division may treat the corporation as resident and assess RMI-source income tax under the Income Tax Act, together with statutory interest and late-filing penalties. Fraudulent or negligent customs declarations for physical exports may attract fines, forfeiture, and other penalties under the Customs Act. There are no retrospective VAT clawbacks because no input/output VAT mechanism exists.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank exists in the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI). The US Dollar is the sole lawful currency and circulates freely under the Compact of Free Association, so monetary conditions are set de facto by the US Federal Reserve and US Treasury clearing and sanctions rules. Banking and foreign-exchange supervision is performed by the Banking Commissioner within the RMI Ministry of Finance under the Banking Act 1989 (as amended), with AML/CFT enforcement anchored in the Anti-Money Laundering Act 2005 (as amended).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMI is a fully dollarized, single-currency jurisdiction, rendering the classic current-account versus capital-account convertibility divide legally immaterial: all payments, royalties, dividends, loan advances and equity injections are freely convertible and transferable in USD without quantitative limits, central approval, or surrender mechanisms. The RMI has been an IMF member with Article VIII obligations since 1992, confirming the commitment to refrain from restrictions on payments and transfers. Profit remittance hurdles are therefore nonexistent in RMI statute; the only practical friction arises from correspondent-bank compliance when USD is cleared through US hub banks, not from any domestic exchange-control barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender rules exist. There is no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, repatriation quota, or surrender obligation applicable to export receipts or cross-border receivables. All USD royalties, distribution fees, placement-agent commissions and ancillary income derived from the ISIC 5911 film-licensing business may be retained in offshore or onshore accounts at the entity's sole discretion, subject only to general record-keeping and AML/CFT documentation duties under the Banking Act and the Anti-Money Laundering Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Marshall Islands (BOMI) - Majuro Head Office

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for a non-resident Marshall Islands Business Corporation. Major digital EMIs and challenger platforms (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, Mercury) generally decline RMI-incorporated legal entities, treat them as elevated-risk due to residual FATF/APG and EU monitoring flags, or impose enhanced due diligence requiring a relationship-bank reference and audited financials. Legally, EMIs are not licensed deposit-taking institutions under the RMI Banking Act 1989 and cannot provide on-island settlement accounts; offshore money-transmitter licenses have no effect on RMI clearing. Recommended structure: maintain the master treasury account with BOMI, and if streaming-platform collections require it, use a segregated EMI collection wallet only as a zero-balance sweep conduit into BOMI; no core cross-border treasury function should sit with an EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is statutorily permissible; no RMI regulation requires directors or ultimate beneficial owners to appear physically for a standard corporate account. Banks accept a KYC dossier transmitted by a licensed RMI Registered Agent comprising notarized and, where applicable, apostilled corporate charters, certified by-laws, a register of directors and shareholders, and a notarized operating resolution. In practice, a video-conference interview with the UBO is mandatory under enhanced due diligence for non-resident corporations, and in-person attendance may be demanded where country-risk flags or source-of-funds opacity arise. A resident director may also be appointed under a limited power of attorney to satisfy local-reachability expectations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: RMI residual country-risk flags from FATF/APG mutual evaluation follow-up and periodic inclusion on international monitoring lists, triggering automatic negative scoring in correspondent credit-decisioning and high-risk client categorization by the onboarding bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance pack containing: (i) current RMI Beneficial Ownership Register certificate; (ii) FATCA/CRS registration confirmation with a valid foreign TIN; (iii) certificate of good standing from the RMI Registrar of Corporations; (iv) licensed-registered-agent letter explaining the commercial purpose; (v) clean OFAC/US/EU sanctions screening of all directors and shareholders; (vi) an independent risk-narrative memorandum classifying ISIC 5911 film licensing as a low-risk IP monetization model; and (vii) a three-year transaction and counterparty-geography forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote-formation shell pattern: a Business Corporation with no employees, no physical premises, and a first-ever account opening shortly after incorporation is automatically flagged as a potential vehicle for IP-trade layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Majuro registered-office lease or virtual-office agreement with the registered agent; board meeting minutes recorded in the RMI; biographical profiles of all directors and UBOs; reviewed or audited financial statements, or a CPA-prepared opening statement of assets; executed licensing contracts evidencing substantive activity; and a notarized declaration of tax-exempt status under the Business Corporation Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, high-volume royalty inflows to a newly opened account from streaming platforms and foreign sub-licensees without visible commercial documentation, a typology associated with layering and shell-company trade laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execution copies of the master distribution agreement and territorial sub-license contracts; chain-of-title manifest with ISAN/EIDR registration numbers; invoices and monthly royalty statements issued to licensees; copyright registration certificates; a UBO source-of-funds declaration certified by the registered agent; and an anticipated-activity profile feeding ongoing transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: USD correspondent refusal: upstream US clearing banks reject the instruction because the beneficiary is an offshore BC and the SWIFT fields show no clear commercial link.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-cleared global treasury due-diligence file: BOMI or Bank of Guam customer-risk assessment confirming the Low_Risk_Standard rating; RMI tax-exemption certificate; evidence of no local taxable presence; confirmation that counterparties are reputable platforms and distributors; and a board-approved beneficial-ownership attestation matching the RMI Beneficial Ownership Register.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan funding is executed by SWIFT MT103/MT202 routed to BOMI's US correspondent, with a compliant Field 70 purpose narrative, e.g., 'Shareholder capital contribution - ISIC 5911 film licensing BC' or 'Shareholder loan per board resolution'. The RMI prescribes no exchange-control declaration or central-bank registration. The receiving bank verifies the injection via a board resolution, amended share register or loan agreement, plus a UBO tax-identification reference, to satisfy correspondent CDD and OFAC screening. Capital escrow lines used for co-production financing must be flagged 'Escrow - Film Licensing' to avoid misclassification as trading receipts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing rails comprise: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for royalty repartition to co-producers, distributors and streaming partners, carrying the underlying invoice or royalty-statement reference; (ii) commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 issued via MT700 where the licensing agreement triggers physical deliverables, requiring commercial invoice, licensing-grant confirmation and shipping/packing list; and (iii) bank cheques or automated debits for on-island Majuro expenses. All instructions must carry sanitized, OFAC-compliant beneficiary data; any payment to a sanctioned state or blocked account triggers an automatic freeze under the Banking Act and correspondent agreements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards (USD versus EUR, GBP, AUD) with a maximum tenor of 12 months, offered by licensed RMI banks or booked through BOMI's US correspondent, permitted solely to hedge documentary royalty receivables and never for speculative trading.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) concluded under a standard ISDA master agreement by a foreign treasury affiliate of the shareholder, permissible for converting non-USD revenue streams into USD with full collateral posting at the counterparty level.

Rolling spot-forward hedges executed onshore for EU/UK receivables above USD 1 million per deal. Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not applicable in the RMI because USD is the official lawful tender and no onshore non-deliverable market exists; hedging of exotic or restricted currencies must be conducted offshore and documented outside the RMI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations (administered through International Registries, Inc.) via the appointed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and March 31 for the preceding calendar year reporting period; statutory filing deadline is March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 10% late penalty accrues on the unpaid annual report fee immediately after March 31; continued non-filing following default notice permits the Registrar to administratively strike off the corporation from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Register Update for film intellectual property holding entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Appointed Marshall Islands registered agent maintaining the Beneficial Ownership Register at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 aligned with the Annual Report cycle; mandatory update within 30 days after any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain an accurate Beneficial Ownership Register or to submit the annual confirmation constitutes a statutory default under the Business Corporations Act; non-compliance may subject the corporation to monetary sanctions and commencement of strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for an unlisted non-resident Business Corporation; a mandatory independent audit applies only to public issuers, licensed banks, insurance companies, and other regulated financial institutions. The independent film licensing entity (ISIC 5911) has no compulsory statutory audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act prescribes no mandatory accounting framework; IFRS is the prevailing standard for international film licensing entities, with US GAAP equally acceptable where financial statements are voluntarily prepared.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must hold a current Beneficial Ownership Register and obtain annual written confirmation from the corporation during the January-to-March Annual Report cycle; any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be re-confirmed within 30 days, with corresponding updates to the register maintained on site.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Company Minute Book (corporate records retained at the registered office)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,000 – US$2,500 per annum, including registered agent services and Annual Report processing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit requirement; voluntary certified audit typically US$3,500 – US$7,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — A non-resident Business Corporation (BC) incorporated under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (BCA) derives income outside the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI); such offshore income is statutorily excluded from the Income Tax Act 1989 (MIRC Title 54). No Marshall Islands corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or branch profits tax is imposed. Only income sourced within the RMI is taxable, and the target licensing model generates no RMI-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective rate is permanently 0% for the non-resident BC; no tax holidays or preferential deductions are necessary, and none are granted. The BC's only recurring exaction is the annual government license/franchise fee payable to the Registrar of Corporations (minimum USD 100 per the BCA fee schedule, scaled up to USD 1,555 by authorized share capital).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No RMI corporate income tax return is prescribed for a non-resident BC whose income is entirely foreign-source. The RMI Income Tax Act does not designate a form for offshore-exempt entities; no CIT filing is required through any portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Not applicable; a non-resident BC is outside the RMI income tax return system. The only annual fiscal deadline is the BCA license fee due on or before 30 April of each calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: No tax return lines apply to a non-resident BC with no RMI-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not file an RMI income tax return. Maintain source-country documentation proving that all film licensing royalties, synchronization fees, and distribution advances are sourced outside the RMI.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: None applicable for income tax, as no return is required. The failure that matters is non-payment of the annual BCA license fee, addressed below.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual License Fee notification — BCA Section 60; filed electronically through the RMI Registrar of Corporations (Department of the Registrar) via a licensed registered agent's portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before 30 April of each year; a newly incorporated BC pays pro-rata at incorporation and thereafter annually by 30 April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name of the Business Corporation as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Name must exactly match the certificate; any foreign-language trade name used in film contracts must be disclosed to the agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The unique RC number assigned by the RMI Registrar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required for fee posting and for the agent's compliance record.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of authorized shares and par value; drives the statutory fee tier (USD 100 for ≤2,500 shares; USD 255 for 2,501–10,000; USD 355 for 10,001–25,000; USD 555 for 25,001–1,000,000; increments to a USD 1,555 cap).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the film investment structure later increases authorized capital, the fee is recalculated for the next fee year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The RMI-licensed registered agent certifies the payment and the entity's good standing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident BC must keep the agent funded; failure of the agent to pay on time exposes the BC to strike-off.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: A USD 100 late penalty is added for payment after 30 April; continued default leads to suspension of the certificate of good standing, administrative strike-off, and loss of authority to transact business. Directors who transact business after dissolution become jointly liable for contracts and debts under the BCA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Economic Substance Notification and Return — the Economic Substance Regulations 2019/2020; submitted electronically by the registered agent to the RMI Registrar in the prescribed ESR form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Notification within 6 months of the end of the financial period and full ESR report within 12 months of the financial period end; the financial period is typically the calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity name, registration number, financial period, and confirmation of tax residency status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare that the entity is not tax-resident in the RMI for income tax purposes; the ESR regime still applies because the entity is incorporated in the RMI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant activity classification: 'Intellectual Property Business', 'Distribution and Service Centre', or 'Holding Company'. Independent film licensing must be disclosed as an IP business or distribution activity, not as a pure holding company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A film licensing BC cannot claim the 'pure equity holding' exemption; it must prove substance in the RMI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of where CIGA are performed: negotiation and execution of license agreements, chain-of-title verification, royalty collection, and enforcement of copyright.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The RMI has no offices or personnel for film licensing; the entity must document that CIGA are performed in the RMI by local directors/employees, which is factually difficult and is the principal ESR exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of full-time RMI employees (Box D1); RMI premises occupied (Box D2); annual operating expenditure in the RMI (Box D3); location of board meetings and management control (Box D4).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Test the entity's practical substance: typically zero employees, no premises, and no spending in Majuro; the entity will fail the statutory test.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Falsification of the ESR return attracts a penalty of up to USD 10,000 plus daily default fines; the Registrar may strike off the BC; adverse information is automatically exchanged with the EU and OECD, which may trigger blacklisting of the corporate structure with foreign banking correspondents.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — The RMI does not impose corporate withholding taxes. Dividends, distributions, deemed distributions, and liquidating proceeds paid by an RMI Business Corporation to its shareholders, whether resident or non-resident, are free of RMI withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI has no comprehensive double tax agreement (DTA) network. There is no internal 'treaty relief' procedure because the domestic rate is already zero. A foreign shareholder resident in a jurisdiction with a DTA with the payor's country cannot invoke an RMI treaty, as none exists. Where the payor of film royalties sits in a foreign country (e.g., a US distributor), that country applies its own domestic withholding and the RMI BC cannot claim treaty shelter absent a DTA; the only protocol is to structure the payment chain through a jurisdiction whose treaty reduces the source-country withholding, causing substance and anti-abuse risk.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: RMI statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid outbound to non-residents is 0%; however, source-country withholding remains a critical practical burden: film licensing royalties paid by a US licensee to the RMI BC are US-source FDAP income subject to 30% US withholding under IRC Sections 871(a)/881(a); because the RMI has no US income tax treaty, no reduction is available. Royalties from EU payers are likewise subject to local withholding (typically 0–30%) depending on the payor state's domestic law, with no RMI treaty relief. Interest income earned by the BC on shareholder loans is exempt from RMI tax and from RMI withholding, but the RMI BC should document that it has no RMI financial institution presence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable — the RMI has not enacted statutory Transfer Pricing (Local File/Master File) documentation rules for tax-exempt non-resident BCs. The official currency is the United States Dollar (USD), but no local-currency threshold exists in the RMI Internal Revenue Code or BCA. Nevertheless, a multinational group whose consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 750 million is expected to file Country-by-Country data under the RMI's commitment to the OECD BEPS framework if the RMI entity is a constituent entity, but in practice the offshore filming licensing BC has no RMI filing trigger because it is not tax-resident and earns no RMI-source income.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI International Tax (Economic Substance) Regulations 2019/2020 (ESR) apply to every entity incorporated in the RMI carrying on a 'relevant activity'. A BC engaged in independent film copyright licensing is classified as an Intellectual Property Business (or Distribution and Service Centre) and is squarely within the ESR. The entity must demonstrate, in the RMI: (1) management and control exercised by RMI-resident directors; (2) full-time employees adequate for the volume of licensing; (3) premises suitable for activity; and (4) operating expenditure proportionate to the royalty income. An IP company enjoying a 'high-risk' category must also show the absence of offshore 'outsourcing' of core income-generating activities unless outsourced to RMI-connected parties with supervisory control in the RMI. The 'pure holding company' exemption is unavailable for active film licensing. In practice, the target structure fails the test because CIGA (contract negotiation, copyright enforcement, collection) occur in the United States or Europe; the RMI structure must therefore be substantiated or restructured.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Economic Substance (ESR) Evasion — Shell IP Company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the BC as a pure shell: no RMI directors, no RMI premises, no local employees, no local expenditure; the BC books foreign film royalties but files an ESR return falsely claiming 'pure holding company' status or denying that it carries a relevant activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of up to USD 10,000 per false ESR filing plus daily default fines; the Registrar may strike off the BC; adverse exchange of information with the EU Code of Conduct Group and the OECD; the BC's tax-exempt status is prospectively cancelled, and the entire accumulated royalty reserve becomes taxable under the domestic law (if RMI-source recharacterized) or the entity is dissolved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, nominees, and the RMI registered agent who sign or procure a false ESR declaration are jointly and severally liable to penalties; the Registrar can commence criminal proceedings for false statements, issue travel restrictions preventing directors from leaving the RMI, and impose restitution of the entity's assets to the Registrar upon strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: International Tax Evasion Facilitation — Sham Film Licensing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fabricating film IP chain-of-title, back-dating license agreements, issuing shell SPVs with nominee shareholders, and using the RMI BC as an instrumentality to conceal the true US or European beneficial owner from his or her home-country tax authority; licensing royalties are deliberately diverted from the actual creator/producer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI Criminal Code (MIRC Title 9) criminalizes forgery, false statements, and conspiracy to defraud revenue: imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to USD 50,000 per count; forfeiture of the royalty proceeds as proceeds of crime; the Registrar can strike off the entity and the foreign tax authority can request mutual legal assistance through the RMI Attorney-General.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced wherever the BC is found to be a mere facade; directors and shadow directors are personally liable for restitution of all diverted copyright royalties and any foreign tax, penalties, and interest the true owner evaded; courts may detain passports, impose travel bans, and commit directors for contempt for up to 6 months pending asset recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: US-Source Withholding Tax Leakage and CFC/Recharacterization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: RMI BC licenses US film rights to a US distributor and the distributor remits gross royalties without applying 30% FDAP withholding; or a US creator transfers the film IP to the RMI BC at zero or nominal consideration; or the BC charges a mark-up for licensed IP that is not at arm's length, without a CUP or residual profit split.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The US licensee is liable as withholding agent for 30% of gross US-source film royalties, plus interest and failure-to-withhold penalties; for the US transferor, IRC Section 367(d) recasts the IP transfer into a deemed annual royalty taxable as US-source income; IRC Section 482 reallocates the BC's profit; the RMI BC is not a CFC because it pays no RMI tax, so all tested income flows to US shareholders as GILTI inclusions (subject to a 10.5% minimum US tax); no treaty relief exists because the RMI has no US DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: US persons who are officers of the US withholding agent face a 100% responsible person penalty under IRC Section 6672 for unpaid withheld taxes; US controlling shareholders of the RMI BC face the GILTI/subpart-F inclusion on their individual returns, civil fraud penalties up to 75%, and criminal tax prosecution with imprisonment; RMI directors who cause the false 'gross remittance' letter to the US distributor are treated as aiders and abettors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT and Beneficial Ownership Failures — Sanctions and Piracy Exposure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the BC to collect payments from sanctioned broadcasters (e.g., state-linked entities in sanctioned jurisdictions), laundering proceeds of film piracy, or settling transactions via SWIFT wire and letters of credit without maintaining the statutory beneficial ownership registry; also failing to register the ultimate human owner with the RMI Registrar under the Beneficial Ownership Regulations applicable to business corporations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI anti-money laundering legislation criminalizes laundering criminal proceeds with imprisonment up to 20 years and fines; the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit may freeze the BC's bank accounts; failure to file beneficial ownership data attracts monetary penalties of up to USD 5,000 and administrative strike-off; violations of UN sanctions trigger asset-freeze and international shipping/banking bans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners, and any non-resident nominee who facilitates payment routing through a third-party account are prosecutable for money laundering, even if the act occurred offshore; RMI courts grant asset preservation orders and travel bans; upon conviction, directors face imprisonment and confiscation of the BC's intellectual property and royalty receivables.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The RMI BC holds film IP as a passive Non-Financial Entity (NFE) and its bank directs the BC to complete CRS self-certification; the true US beneficial owner is undisclosed, or the BC incorrectly certifies itself as a Non-Reporting Financial Institution to avoid CRS reporting, while maintaining a US controlling person's account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The RMI has in force a Model-1 IGA with the US and CRS exchange arrangements; the RMI bank must report the controlling US person to the RMI Competent Authority, which automatically exchanges the information with the IRS; mis-certification triggers a USD 10,000 penalty under CRS rules, reporting leakage, and a Category-4 or Category-6 audit risk classification by the RMI financial intelligence unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing a false CRS self-certification are personally liable for penalties and for any loss to the entity or its shareholders caused by the resulting disclosure; the beneficial owner's undisclosed accounts are exposed to US FBAR and FATCA penalties (starting at USD 10,000 per account, rising to 50% of the account balance for willful violations), alongside potential criminal referral.
